question: The remainder when the product \(1492 \cdot 1776 \cdot 1812 \cdot 1996\) is divided by \(5\) is
solution:
Only the ones digits of the factors affect the ones digit of their product. To see why, split each factor into its ones digit and a multiple of \(10\). When multiplying, every contribution involving one of those multiples is itself a multiple of \(10\).

The ones digits of the four factors are \(2,6,2,6\), and
\[
2\cdot6\cdot2\cdot6=144.
\]
Thus the original product ends in \(4\). Subtracting \(4\) leaves a multiple of \(10\), which is divisible by \(5\). Since \(4<5\), the required remainder is \(4\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
